v1.feedback: The whoosh concept lands — the depth-staggered shearing wave across the head is legible and the Balla speed-line ellipse stretch in the fragment shader is a nice touch that ties the futurist reference to the motion. The porcelain-to-amber palette shift during the whoosh is restrained and warm. Two things to tighten: the whoosh currently reads as a single lateral gust that resolves back to rest, but the cycling repeat flattens the drama — consider making the return path asymmetric (slower re-settle with overshoot/wobble) so each cycle feels earned rather than looped. Second, the point sizes during the static phase are a bit uniform and fine-grained, making the resting head read slightly soft; vary rest-state size by curvature or normal angle to give the face more sculptural contrast even before the whoosh fires.

v2.feedback: The whoosh concept lands — depth-staggered lateral shear with amber tint and Balla-style speed-line ellipses is a legit formal idea, not just a variable rename. But the swerve feels timid: the shear magnitude and fan-out are modest enough that at rest the piece is just another Lee Perry Smith point cloud, and during whoosh it reads more like a glitch than a Futurist force-line painting. Push the whoosh harder — let the shear fully decompose the silhouette into horizontal streaks before reconverging, so the head is genuinely unreadable mid-motion and the 'surprise' earns its name. The palette shift to amber is nice but could benefit from a secondary cool accent (steel blue trail on the trailing edge) to give the motion directionality rather than a uniform wash.
